security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation placeholders, Markdown code fences, SDK session identifiers, or expected file and network examples. The unsafe eval examples are confirmed because they evaluate agent-controlled tool-call arguments, and the skill manifest grants broad Bash access. No prompt injection indicators were found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Unsafe eval examples evaluate tool-call input.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a constrained math parser, an explicit operation allowlist, or a sandboxed evaluator with strict limits.

remediation.issue: The manifest allows broad Python command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash(python *) from allowed tools or narrow it to specific commands needed for documented setup.

remediation.issue: Webhook examples can send data to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for destination allowlists, stored secrets, human approval, and payload minimization before enabling webhook tools.

content.user_title: Build Python Apps with inference.sh SDK
content.value_statement: Python teams need reliable patterns for inference.sh integrations. This skill explains SDK setup, async workflows, files, streaming, agents, and tool building.
actual_capabilities: Explains installation and authentication for the inferencesh Python package.
Shows synchronous and asynchronous app execution patterns.
Documents file upload, download, temporary file, and attachment workflows.
Covers agent creation, reusable skills, tool calls, and human approval patterns.
Describes streaming progress, sessions, retries, and concurrency controls.
Introduces tool builder types for client, app, agent, webhook, and internal tools.
limitations: It is documentation and examples, not a runnable SDK implementation.
Examples use placeholder API keys and app names that users must replace.
Security-sensitive examples require review before production use.
The skill does not verify current inference.sh service availability or pricing.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI App Calls
use_cases.description: Learn how to run inference.sh apps from Python with inputs, outputs, and streaming progress.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Use agent, tool, session, and approval examples to design multi-step assistant workflows.

use_cases.title: Integrate Files and Async Jobs
use_cases.description: Apply file upload, download, concurrency, retry, and timeout patterns in backend services.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the simplest safe way to install the inferencesh package, configure an API key, and run one app call.

prompt_templates.title: Add Files and Streaming
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Python workflow that uploads an image, runs an inference.sh app, streams progress, and saves the result safely.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Agent with Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating an inference.sh agent with a client tool, an app tool, and human approval for sensitive actions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned inference.sh Python SDK architecture for async concurrency, session reuse, file handling, secrets, and tool-call safety.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to run one inference.sh app from Python.
output_examples.output: A concise setup path with package installation, API key handling, one app call, and result inspection steps.

output_examples.input: An agent engineer asks how to add tools to an assistant.
output: Recommended tool categories for the workflow.
Notes about validating tool arguments before execution.

output_examples.input: A backend team asks how to process many jobs concurrently.
output_examples.output: An async workflow outline with concurrency limits, timeout handling, retries, and result aggregation guidance.

best_practices: Store API keys in environment variables or a secret manager, not in source files.
Require approval and argument validation for tools that write files, call webhooks, or run code.
Limit async concurrency and session lifetimes to control cost and resource usage.
anti_patterns: Do not copy examples that evaluate tool-call text as code.
Do not expose uploaded files publicly unless the workflow requires public access.
Do not send model or tool outputs to external webhooks without an allowlist and user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill install the Python SDK automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents installation commands and usage patterns for the inferencesh package.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include async examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers async clients, streaming, concurrency limits, timeouts, retries, and web framework integration.

faq.question: Does it cover file uploads?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents automatic uploads, manual uploads, file attachments, downloads, and temporary files.

faq.question: Are the API keys in the examples real?
faq.answer: No. The examples use placeholders and also show environment variable based configuration.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review tool-call execution, webhook destinations, file permissions, API key handling, and any code execution settings.
